payload.rationale: The root cause is that `slugify` in src/text.js line 11 calls `.replace(/[\s-]+/, '-')` with a non-global regex. JavaScript's String.prototype.replace only replaces the first match of a non-global regex, so after the first whitespace/dash run is converted to a dash, all subsequent runs are left as-is (e.g. 'hello big  world' -> 'hello-big  world'). Adding the `g` flag makes the replacement apply to every `[\s-]+` run, so all words are joined by single dashes, matching the documented behavior ('words joined by single dashes') and the expectations in test/text.test.js. This is consistent with the neighboring regexes on lines 10 and 12, which already use the `g` flag.
